items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: And he would play, (singing) da-da-de-da-de-la. That was part of his thing. He lived across the street from Paul Desmond for a while, by the way, Henny Youngman. He used to (unintelligible). So what I thought was funny was that in the waiting room, Henny Youngman would go to use the phone and he would just leave his fiddle sitting there like a… (laughs) It probably cost $15 or something. So… and I think in those days I could carry my guitar on the plane. So I got on the plane. I put the guitar, and here comes…
No. But how was he as a jazz player?
